name: AlgoLaser DIY Kit MK3
tagline: Open-frame 400 × 400 mm diode with a standalone touchscreen, sold with 8W, 15W or 20W modules
tldr: The DIY Kit MK3 is AlgoLaser's third-generation open-frame kit, launched in July 2026: a 400 × 400 mm frame that arrives 95% pre-assembled, a capacitive touchscreen running AlgoOS for offline jobs, a flip-down focus stick and 15,000 mm/min engraving. It is sold with an 8W, 15W or 20W diode module, from $259. Open a power tier for exact prices and benchmarks.
mainObjective: Budget open-frame engraving and cutting on a mid-size bed, without a computer for simple jobs

priceRange.note: Official AlgoLaser store, Oct 2026: $259 (8W machine) to $659 (20W Basic kit); the Basic kit adds a honeycomb, RR2 rotary roller and riser kit

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood & plywood (3 mm on every module; up to 12 mm claimed on the 20W)
cannot: Bare metal (no infrared module listed for the MK3)
Enclosed use without the optional enclosure

pros: 400 × 400 mm bed from $259, 95% pre-assembled with a five-step setup
Capacitive touchscreen with AlgoOS: text, sketches and stored projects run without a computer
Same frame for all three modules, plus LightBurn and LaserGRBL support
cons: Open frame: no enclosure, and the Class 1 enclosure is a $299 extra
AlgoLaser publishes no spot size, optical power test or cutting figure except 12 mm for the 20W
Launched in July 2026 with no independent review yet
beginnerNotes: Choose the power before anything else: the 8W engraves fine detail but cuts slowly, the 15W is the balanced choice, and the 20W is the one for regular cutting. The Basic kit adds a honeycomb, a rotary roller and risers for $200; check whether you need them before paying for them.
proTips: Use the flip-down focus stick before every job and check the frame is square after shipping. The touchscreen is handy for text and stored projects; for photos and complex vector work, LightBurn gives finer control. Plan for air assist on any module you cut with, and for an outdoor exhaust.
primaryUse: Budget open-frame diode engraving and cutting with standalone touchscreen control

faq.question: What changed from the DIY Kit MK2?
faq.answer: The MK3 adds a capacitive touchscreen running AlgoOS for offline jobs, a flip-down focus stick and a 95% pre-assembled frame. AlgoLaser claims up to 60% more power than the previous kit and engraving at 15,000 mm/min. The 400 × 400 mm work area is unchanged.

faq.question: Which module should I choose?
faq.answer: The 8W ($259, October 2026) is for detailed engraving and light cutting, the 15W ($309) is the all-rounder, and the 20W ($459 with a free air pump) is for regular wood cutting, where AlgoLaser claims 12 mm in one pass. Open each tier for its benchmark.

faq.question: Can the DIY Kit MK3 be enclosed?
faq.answer: Yes, with AlgoLaser's Smart Enclosure 2.0 with camera, sold for $299 on the official store in October 2026, plus an optional $299 smoke purifier. Without it, the MK3 is an open-frame laser: wear the supplied glasses, keep it away from children and vent the smoke outside.

moduleSystem.headline: Three diode modules on the same MK3 frame
moduleSystem.description: The DIY Kit MK3 is sold with an 8W, 15W or 20W diode module on the same 400 × 400 mm frame and touchscreen. The power is chosen at purchase; modules fit the same head mount, one at a time.

editorialDepth.advantages: The MK3 keeps the low price and 400 × 400 mm bed of AlgoLaser's kits and adds what beginners usually miss: a near-assembled frame, a touchscreen that runs jobs without a computer and a focus stick built into the head. Three modules cover everything from detailed engraving to regular cutting.
editorialDepth.limitations: It remains an open-frame diode: safety, smoke and enclosure are extra costs. AlgoLaser gives few verifiable figures, and no independent review has tested the frame, the modules or the touchscreen yet.

standoutFeatures.title: Touchscreen that works offline
standoutFeatures.body: AlgoOS runs text, sketches and more than 400 stored projects straight from the capacitive screen, with no computer or app needed.

standoutFeatures.title: 95% pre-assembled frame
standoutFeatures.body: The frame arrives nearly assembled and is set up in five steps, which AlgoLaser puts at under 10 minutes.
